subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open dirty fork PR, close it and queue a fresh same-repo fix, or keep waiting on that branch?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but an open cross-repository PR still uses closing syntax for this issue, is dirty, and cannot be maintainer-modified, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the dirty fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix for title sanitization, displayName precedence, and regression proof.

options.title: Adopt And Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Ask a maintainer or contributor to rebase the fork branch, cover both current title hydration paths, and add real TUI/Gateway proof before review.

options.title: Wait On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork branch despite its dirty merge state and lack of maintainer-modify permissions.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the dirty fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix for title sanitization, displayName precedence, and regression proof.
